problems.title: Point and Capture
problems.goal: White's stone at D4 is boxed in on three sides and down to one liberty. Play the capturing move.
problems.failNote: Any move other than E4 leaves White's last liberty open, and the stone lives to be defended next turn.

problems.title: Capture the Pair
problems.goal: White's two connected stones at D4 and E4 share one last liberty. Play it to capture both at once.
problems.failNote: White's pair keeps its one shared liberty until F4 is taken; anything else lets the group breathe again.

problems.title: Escape by Capturing
problems.goal: Black's stone at E4 is in atari with one liberty, F4. Playing there both saves the stone and takes a White stone next door off the board — find it.
problems.failNote: Anywhere but F4 leaves Black's stone with no liberty left to take; White removes it on the next move.

problems.title: Extend to Safety
problems.goal: Black's two stones on the edge are in atari, down to one liberty at A6. Extend there to reach new liberties and escape.
problems.failNote: Anywhere but A6 leaves Black's pair at one liberty; White captures it next turn.

problems.title: Split the Eye Space
problems.goal: Black's group has one place left to live: the three-point straight run A7-B7-C7 along the bottom edge. Play its center point to split the run into two separate eyes.
problems.failNote: Playing A7 or C7 instead leaves the run as one connected two-point space — roomy, but still only one eye, and White can eventually reduce it to nothing.

problems.title: Deny the Second Eye
problems.goal: White's only potential eye space is the three-point straight run A7-B7-C7. Play its center point so the run can never become two separate eyes.

B7.note: White tries to capture the invading stone by filling around it, but that only spends White's own last liberties. Black's C7 takes the entire White group off the board.

problems.failNote: Playing A7 or C7 instead of the center leaves the run as one connected two-point space bordering only White — still a single potential eye, not yet denied.

problems.title: Capture the False Eye
problems.goal: Black's corner point at A1 looks like an eye, but White's stone at B2 — the corner's only diagonal — makes it false. Capture that stone at its last liberty to make the eye real.
problems.failNote: Leaving White's stone on the board keeps the corner's only diagonal in enemy hands; the eye at A1 stays false, and White can eventually force it to fill.

problems.title: Split the Bent Eye Space
problems.goal: Black's group again has one life-giving shape: a bent three-point space at F7-G7-G6, wrapped around the board corner. Play the corner point to split it into two eyes.
problems.failNote: Playing F7 or G6 instead leaves the bend as one connected space — still just one eye, and still vulnerable.

problems.title: Deny the Bent Eye Space
problems.goal: White's only potential life is the bent three-point space F7-G7-G6. Play its corner point so it can never split into two eyes.

G7.note: White tries to capture the invading stone by filling around it, but each fill only spends White's own last liberties. Black's G6 takes the entire White group off the board.

problems.failNote: Playing F7 or G6 instead of the corner leaves the bend as one connected space bordering only White — still a single potential eye, not yet denied.

problems.title: Play the Biggest Point
problems.goal: Two moves are open: capturing White's pair at C2-D2 in the corner, or filling the single neutral point at G7. Count them and play the bigger one.

E2.note: White tries to reoccupy the captured pocket, but the stone has only one liberty there; Black's D2 removes it again for good.

problems.failNote: G7 is worth one point however it's filled; capturing at E2 is worth several times that once both the prisoners and the freed territory are counted.

problems.title: Take the Dame
problems.goal: A1 is the last open point on the board, bordered by both colors — a dame, nobody's territory under territory scoring. Play it anyway: under area scoring every point you claim still counts.
problems.failNote: Leaving A1 open costs nothing under territory scoring, but if White takes it instead, the area-scoring margin swings two full points against Black.

problems.title: Recognize the Finish
problems.goal: Black's corner point at A1 is already secure territory, and nothing else on the board is worth a move. Pass.
problems.failNote: Playing inside your own settled territory at A1 gains nothing under area scoring, and it costs a real point under territory scoring — the point stops counting as territory and no capture replaces it.
